newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OECD sees Austria budget deficit at 3 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees Austria budget deficit at 3 pct in 1997.

text.p: Austria is set to reach the Maastricht budget deficit target of three percent of GDP in 1997, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development said in a survey on Thursday.
However, the Paris-based think tank forecast the budget deficit would climb back up to 3.4 percent in 1998. Last year the budget deficit stood at 4.3 percent.

Austria has passed austerity budgets for both 1996 and 1997 in a bid to bring its excessive budget deficit down to the three percent of GDP stipulated by the Maastricht criteria for European economic and monetary union.
"The OECD has praised Austria...saying it will reach its budget target," Chancellor Viktor Klima told a news conference on the presentation of the OECD survey.

The survey said Austria was poised for "moderate growth" of 1.4 percent for 1997, compared to 1.1 percent last year. Strong private consumption and rising exports was likely to spur GDP growth to 2.3 percent in 1998, it noted.
Inflation is expected to slide to 1.8 percent this year from 1.9 percent in 1997, declining further to 1.7 percent next year.
The OECD forecast a slight decrease in the jobless rate for 1998 to 6.4 percent from an expected 6.5 percent in 1997 and 6.2 percent in 1996.
The overall deficit is seen widening to around 75 percent in 1998 from 69 percent in 1995, in spite of lower expenditure and higher revenues.
The forecast rise showed "what (can) happen if nothing is done", Klima said. "Something will be done," he added.
He said there would be a reversal of the upward trend in the overall deficit in 1997 as a result of privatisations, sale of debt and "interpretations in line with the Maastricht Treaty".
Klima also promised to follow a "very disciplined tax policy without further burdening the population".
